files.deductions: The two bindings require editing to add an entry point (P2); this is a thin binding over substantial hidden core behavior (P11).
A new namespace needs a declaration (P2). Checked schemas are stateless; the parsing/recovery boundary is not named here (P10).
New failure categories edit a closed union (P2); useful shared declaration, little hidden behavior (P11).
Public export additions require editing this declaration list (P2). The boundary hides core topology and private policies.
Shipped operations require schema additions (P2). The planner owns recovery, but these schema declarations do not name it at each entry (P10).
Shape additions edit the schema (P2); stateless schema definitions leave recovery ownership to the callable boundary (P10).
Content extension adds a schema variant (P2). Core validation/Authoring recovery is not stated at these individual schema entries (P10).
New intent shapes edit declarations (P2). Schemas have no effects but do not name the recovery boundary (P10).
New object variants edit the declaration (P2). Safe parsing/commit ownership is documented at the public API rather than this schema (P10).
New connection variants edit declarations (P2). Stateless schema recovery boundary unnamed locally (P10).
New section variants require schema edits (P2). These declarations leave error/recovery ownership to Model API docs (P10).
New impact namespaces edit Target (P2). Impact.id is an unbranded reporting identity (P5); thin shared outcome declarations (P11).
Additional dependency-bearing content adds an explicit cleanup step (P2); current cleanup decisions are named and ordered.
New cleanup steps require an orchestrator edit (P2); the entry coordinates six local view concerns despite named intermediate values (P7).
Additional namespaces/metadata fields edit this step list (P2); consumes the unbranded Impact.id report contract (P5). JSON.stringify equality remains less explicit about object-key ordering (P7).
Handlers live in a fixed local table (P2). Repeated narrow-or-reject guard idiom appears in more than three table entries (P6); no cast hides the union correlation.
Batch stages require an orchestration edit (P2). The retained public catch maps all thrown causes to a generic shape diagnostic, limiting tracing (P7).
New override categories edit the coordinated transforms (P2). Four core exports expose preservation/reset operations, broader than one entry (P11); the leaf placement helper is private.
Fixed namespace writer table requires updates (P2). Repeated namespace guard/writer assembly idiom across five writers receives the literal DRY dock (P6).
Namespace removal and cascade step lists are closed (P2). JSON serialization used to detect nontrivial dependency cleanup is less direct than an explicit change set (P7).
New view operation kinds require editing the applySectionEdit conditional chain (P2=0). Remaining steps have explicit names, results and recovery documentation.
Key and path policies come from callers; a real but thin identity algorithm (P11).
Small recursive utility hides real but thin behavior (P11); entry explicitly requires detached acyclic input.
Fixed namespace step list (P2); thin scope policy over the duplicate algorithm (P11).
Input guard stages require source edits (P2). The explicit traversal queue still requires tracing several stages (P7). Local queue/counter mutation receives the SOP P13=5 anchor.
Parameterized diagnostic constructors share one true-means-failure convention. Entry docs do not all identify recovery ownership (P10); construction is real but thin (P11).
Content rules compose through a list, but new collection-level reference owners require a step edit (P2). Brand types retained throughout address resolution.
Thin library-error translation (P11); the doc does not name the calling validation/plan recovery boundary (P10).
The local validation stage list needs edits for new stages (P2). Retained broad exception mapping loses cause detail (P7); output is still a typed failure, so P9 remains 10.
Adding a rule stage requires an edit (P2). Descendant projection is an extra core surface alongside validation (P11).
Additional key-bearing block variants require changing validateBlockKey conditional dispatch (P2=0). Foreign-key checks still carry six coordinated rule outcomes (P7), now named explicitly.
Allowed kinds are typed table policies; additional validation stages still require editing orchestration (P2). Endpoint lookup is now private.
New containment checks edit the orchestration (P2). Exposes useful ancestry/visibility helpers in addition to validation (P11). Local traversal cursor/set mutation receives P13=5.
New scope/rule steps require edits (P2). Group membership precedence and absent owner semantics are documented and expressed as named steps.
Compatibility data are typed; additional specialized rule stages need edits (P2). visibleRelationships adds a second core surface (P11).
Additional sequence rules need a stage edit (P2). Parent, branch, participant and ordering decisions have separate named helpers.
The validation stage set requires edits to extend (P2). Counts and cycles are independently named; diagnostic order is retained.
Rule arrays compose current behavior, but the fixed group-first stage remains source-owned (P2).
